CLÁR PROGRAMME 
The CLÁR 2025 Programme closed for applications for Measure 1 to Galway County Council 
on May 15th 2025.   Measure 2 and 3 are made direct to the Department of Community and 
Rural Development.  
CLÁR is funding programme for small scale capital investments in community amenities in 
designated CLÁR area in the County. CLÁR covers extensive areas in four Municipal Districts 
and a smaller area of the Athenry-Oranmore District.   It is proposed that the areas in CLÁR 
will be review in 2025 in advance of the 2026 programme.  
The 2025 Scheme was advertised in local print media and GCC social media and via Galway 
County Public Participation Network and details circulated among Elected Members and 
Members of Local Community Development Committee (LCDC). A webinar was held on April 
30th in collaboration with the PPN with morning and evening time slots and over 70 
attendees.  
 A total of 52 applications were submitted the Galway County Council SUBMIT 
grants further to verification eligibility and initial review 27 proposals were 
recommended for further detailed assessment.  Galway County Council can put 
forward a maximum of 16 proposals including one from Gaeltacht community for 
consideration by the Department of Community and Rural Development in

4 
 
advance of June 13th 2025.  The maximum grant level has increased from 50,000 
in 2024 to 65,000k in 2025.  Of the sixteen projects Galway County Council can 
put forward two proposals if eligible for 100k in grant funding.   Grant funding is 
at 90% with 10% matching funding.  
 The facilities and amenities must be freely available (nominal fee acceptable) to 
all members of the community without any additional restrictions or 
requirements being imposed and applicants are asked to have relevant statutory 
permission in place.  
 In line with other Schemes, in the case of capital works, the applicant must own 
or have a 15 year lease in place at the time of application. 
 Decision on the 2025 Scheme are due from the Department by end of September 
2025.  
 Completion and drawdown date for successful projects extended by 6 months 
from 12 months to 18 months approximately to allow for a more substantial 
amount of time for procurement and completion of the works, given the 
increasing scale of the capital fund.

Small scale renovation works to community facilities open to the wider community such as 
community centres/sports centres/clubhouses of sporting groups/youth centres/men’s 
sheds etc. This includes external works such as parking and accessibility enhancements  
 Multi-use gaming areas (MUGAs)/Astro-turf facilities including upgrades

 Walking/running /athletics tracks  
 Handball alleys/tennis courts/basketball courts/cricket grounds/ outdoor bowling 
areas  
 Community gyms/community cinemas  
 Sensory gardens/Community gardens/ allotments/ biodiversity planting  
 Access to unique local heritage sites / areas of natural beauty  
 Enhanced outdoor toilet and changing facilities  
 Car parking  
 Improving access at sports grounds e.g. development/upgrade of spectator stands at 
local sports grounds with a particular focus on improving access for people of all 
abilities and ages   
 Solar Bins

HEALTHY IRELAND FUND 
Men’s Health Week 2025 
Healthy Galway County is actively preparing to participate in Men’s Health Week 2025, 
which will take place from Monday, 9th June to Sunday, 15th June, concluding on Father’s 
Day. This initiative represents a significant opportunity to raise awareness, encourage 
conversations, and promote positive action around men’s health and wellbeing. 
This year’s theme, “Shoulder-to-Shoulder – Connecting for Health,” highlights the 
importance of community and connection in supporting men’s wellbeing. Across Galway 
City and County, a diverse programme of events will offer men the chance to engage, learn, 
and take proactive steps toward better health. 
The key aims of Men’s Health week are to 
heighten awareness of preventable health 
problems affecting males of all ages, support 
men and boys in making healthier lifestyle 
choices and engaging in health-promoting 
activities and encourage early detection and 
treatment of health issues by promoting timely 
access to healthcare services and providing free 
health checks at events. 
A wide-ranging programme of events will take 
place across Galway City and County, offering 
men opportunities to engage, learn, and take 
proactive steps toward better health. Healthy 
County Galway will be actively supporting and participating in several of these events, 
including the Men’s Health Fair at T. O’Higgins Homevalue Hardware in Galway on Monday, 
9th June; a Currach event on Inis Meáin on Tuesday evening; and the launch of an online 
seminar, “Men Supporting Each Other,” on Wednesday, 11th June at 8pm. Also on 
Wednesday, a health information event providing free health checks will be held at Fursa’s 
Parish Hall in Headford. Further activities include the Men’s Health Symposium at the Wild 
Goat Café in Letterfrack on Thursday, 12th June; a community health event at Temperance 
Hall in Loughrea, led by GRD; and a Farmers’ Health Event at Maam Cross Mart on Saturday, 
14th June. 
Healthy County Galway is proud to support and lead several of these initiatives, reinforcing 
our commitment to improving men’s health outcomes and fostering inclusive, health-
conscious communities. In addition to coordinating and participating in events, Healthy 
Galway is actively promoting Men’s Health Week through a comprehensive communications 
campaign. This includes broadcasting key messages and event highlights on local radio 
stations within the county, publishing features in regional newspapers, and engaging 
audiences across social media platforms to maximise reach and community involvement.

The launch of the Dementia Café initiative in Connemara has also gained strong visibility, with

Radio, and RTÉ Raidió na Gaeltachta in addition to social media platforms

FURTHER COMMUNITY EVENTS SUPPORTED BY HEALTHY COUNTY GALWAY COUNTY 
COUNCIL 
The Community Health and Wellbeing Board initiative continues to raise awareness of local 
and national supports and services available to County Galway. This month, several boards 
were delivered to different localities to specifically highlight these supports and services, as 
well as to promote the Five Ways to Wellbeing: Connect, Be Active, Take Notice, Keep 
Learning, and Give. 
 
Some of the clubs and community groups that recently received and displayed their 
community boards include GRETB, Outdoor Activities in Petersburg, Stuntworx Elite in 
Doughiska, St. Cuans Utd in Ahascragh, and the South Galway Special Olympics Club. 
 
Clifden Men's Shed recently celebrated the conclusion of an 8-week Tai Chi and Mindfulness 
course with a Presentation of Certificates Ceremony, followed by a course evaluation and 
refreshments. Congratulations to the 21 shedders and family carers who completed the 
course, held at Clifden District Hospital. This was a great initiative organised by the HSE 
Carers Department and funded by Healthy County Galway. Thank you to everyone who 
participated and supported this journey towards wellness and mindfulness.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT  
AGE FRIENDLY PROGRAMME  
Galway County Council has submitted several projects under various award categories of 
the National Age Friendly Recognition and Achievement Awards, which close for 
applications on 12th June 2025, and has also encouraged partner agencies on the Age 
Friendly Alliance to submit nominations for the awards.   Shortlisting will occur during the 
summer and notifications will issue to the successful projects of judging dates in early 
September.    
 
The first draft of an Age Friendly Strategy 2025-2030 is due to be received from the 
Consultant in June and will be considered at the Older People’s Council (OPC) Meeting on 
19th June, following which further consultations will take place with the Age Friendly 
Alliance, Elected Members, etc., prior to the strategy being brought forward for adoption at 
a Plenary Meeting.  
TIDY TOWNS 
A second tranche of Tidy Towns Groups will be moved over to the local authority insurance 
cover package through Irish Public Bodies (IPB) which will offer a consistent and 
comprehensive insurance cover for their activities.   This Insurance Cover has been agreed 
between local authorities and IPB as a “Thank You” to all Tidy Towns Groups for the valuable 
work they undertake across our towns and villages.    Approximately half of the County’s 
40+ groups had been moved over in April, and further discussions were required with the 
groups in this second tranche prior to processing the changeover.   
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION NETWORK  
The Department of Rural and Community Development have published the Annual Report 
2023 for Public Participation Networks, for which all PPN’s and local authorities submit 
reports and statistics for collation.    The Report shows that Galway County PPN, with 1,268 
Member Groups, is the second-largest PPN in the country, and is also in the top 5 nationally 
for the number of PPN Representatives which sit on various boards and committee 
structures, which correlates directly to the primary purpose of PPN’s which is to increase 
input by local communities into decision-making at local government level.     The PPN 
Support Worker also circulated notification of all local and national consultation 
opportunities, and all open funding and training opportunities, to all PPN Member Groups 
through the June Newsletter.     The PPN Workers will also attend a national Networking 
Meeting on 10th June to discuss upcoming issues for the PPN’s at national and local levels.

Studio Mór is a supported visual art studio providing a safe, accessible and inclusive space

independently or with support to use the space one day a week. 
The deadline for residency applications was 10 January. Studio Mór artists supported by

OUGHTERARD COURTHOUSE SUMMER ARTS PROGRAMME LAUNCH 2025 
 
The Launch of OCAP’s Summer Arts Programme took place 
on Friday 16th June. For Summer 2025 OCAP present 4 
vibrant exhibitions featuring work from 77 artists across the 
West of Ireland. The Season kicks off with the annual group 
show by Uachtar Arts Group. This year, 34 artists draw 
inspiration from the beauty and importance of Lough Corrib, 
a national treasure at the heart of our community. The 
exhibition is the result of the creative journey, including 
learning from the Corrib Catchment Partnership and a boat 
trip to Inchagoill Island with Corrib Cruises.  
The launch was opened by Sharon O’Grady, Arts Officer. The Arts Programme is supported 
by Galway County Council through the Community Support Scheme (Arts Grants) 2025.  
CREATIVE IRELAND 
KINVARA COMMUNITY ORCHESTRA – DANCE OF LIFE 
Over the June Bank Holiday weekend, the Kinvara Community Orchestra delivered 2 sold 
out performances of their show, ‘Dance of Life’. This project, supported under the Galway 
County Council Creative Communities Open Call, consisted of an evening of song, poetry, 
dance, and community. Audiences were treated to a two-hour long performance which 
featured classical, country, traditional, and contemporary music and dance. The strong 
sense of community was palpable in the room as 3 generations took to the stage to share 
their art forms. Special recognition was given to members of the community who had 
passed away in recent months as performances from family members were dedicated to 
their memory.

CONNEMARA BEACH REGAINS PRESTIGIOUS BLUE FLAG AFTER 12-YEAR ABSENCE 
  
In a major boost for the local community and tourism in Connemara, Céibh an Spidéil beach 
has regained its coveted Blue Flag status after losing it in 2013. 
  
The announcement was made today (Friday, 16 May) at the national Blue Flag and Green 
Coast Awards ceremony hosted by An Taisce at the Ravenport Resort in Curracloe, Co. 
Wexford. 
  
The beach is among eight locations in County Galway to receive the prestigious Blue Flag for 
2025, with a further six beaches recognised with Green Coast Awards. 
  
The Blue Flag is an internationally recognised symbol awarded to bathing areas that meet 
exceptional standards in water quality, safety, environmental education, and beach 
management. Alongside Céibh an Spidéil, this year’s Blue Flag recipients include Long Point 
at Loughrea Lake, Portumna bathing area, Trá Inis Oírr, Trá an Dóilín (An Cheathrú Rua), An 
Trá Mhór (Indreabhán), Trá Chill Mhuirbhigh (Inis Mór), and Traught Beach (Kinvara). 
  
Six beaches were also honoured with Green Coast Awards, which recognise clean water and 
pristine natural environments in more remote or less developed areas. The Green Coast 
awardees are Trá Inis Oírr and Trá Poll na gCaorach (Inis Oírr), East End and Dumhach 
(Inishbofin), Aillebrack (Ballyconneely), and Renvyle Beach (Tully). 
  
“County Galway’s beaches are renowned for their clean environment, excellent water 
quality and natural beauty, and we are delighted that once again so many of them have 
received the coveted Blue Flag and Green Coast Awards,” commented Cllr. Martina Kinane, 
Cathaoirleach of the County of Galway. She continued, “These awards are a testament to 
the hard work and dedication of those who clean our beaches.  I am particularly happy to 
see that the beach at Céibh an Spidéil has regained its Blue Flag which will be very much 
welcomed by the local community.”

clean groups for all their hard work and dedication in ensuring our coastline is kept clean.

Measure A8 of the Multi-Annual Rural Water Programme (MARWP) for the provision of 
wastewater infrastructure in the villages of Craughwell and Clarinbridge. The absence of

potential for economic and community development in both locations and this issue is a

Council seeking confirmation that we are in a position to meet the required 15% co-funding 
contribution towards the overall project cost. The financial implications for the Council are 
significant. The estimated minimum contribution required from Galway County Council is 
€3.81 million, but the final figure is estimated to approach €5 million. This level of 
expenditure has not been provided for in the adopted 2025 budget. Any such commitment 
would need to be met from the Council’s own resources under the 2026 Budget Process.

identifiable financial return for the Council. On completion of the project, the infrastructure 
will be handed over to Uisce Éireann, who will assume ownership and operational

such, the Council will be making a substantial upfront investment without any subsequent 
revenue stream or retained control of the assets.

contribution towards the project will be considered under the 2026 budgetary process.

Among the key priorities are conducting a

sensitive habitats such as peatlands and marine ecosystems, while expanding environmental 
education through the Heritage in Schools programme. 
  
The built heritage aspects of the Galway County Heritage and Biodiversity Plan 2024-2030 
aim to preserve, protect, and enhance the county's built and archaeological heritage by 
promoting best practices, supporting community engagement, and ensuring compliance 
with relevant legislation. The plan also seeks to raise awareness, provide education and 
training, and foster collaboration among stakeholders to ensure the sustainable 
management and conservation of these heritage assets. 
  
On the cultural heritage front, the plan aims to empower communities to actively engage 
with and safeguard their local heritage. This involves recording and digitising cultural 
heritage data, supporting community-led arts and oral history projects, and strengthening

Dunmore River Walk is a Community Park located along the bank of the Sinking river and 
linking the town centre to some key community facilities such as playing pitches, numerous 
housing estates, and playground. This is a freely available public space within the town and 
is used by all members of the community on a daily basis, however, the basic infrastructure 
could be improved to maximise accessibility and safety for all members of the community. 
The projects to be undertaken have been identified through consultations with members of 
the local community and respond directly to their identified needs.    
Dept. of Rural & Community, Integration and Environment allocated funding through Clar 
2024 for this project and works commenced in the last month. The project will encompass 3 
main elements:  
• Safety Works to replace fencing along the boundary with the river which has become 
dangerously deficient in places and poses a risk to the public.      
• Accessibility Works to improve the condition and width of walkways to ensure they are 
accessible, allied with the provision of age friendly benches and accessible picnic tables – 
these works will be underpinned by a Walkability Audit conducted with older people to 
maximise accessibility for all.    Additional works to improve the usability of the area for all 
will include provision of bins and signage at strategic locations.  
• Biodiversity Works will also be undertaken as currently the area predominantly comprises 
of grassed areas, therefore, emphasis will be placed on additional planting of native species 
to improve biodiversity and the visual appearance of the amenity.
